benchmarks.label: Most proficient third of a university-student sample
benchmarks.note: Mean sentence-copying speed (IQR 20) for the study's approximately top third by jointly selected speed and accuracy; 435 of 1,301 Aix-Marseille University students, predominantly young French speakers.

benchmarks.label: Least proficient third of a university-student sample
benchmarks.note: Mean sentence-copying speed (IQR 18) for the study's approximately bottom third by jointly selected speed and accuracy; 432 of 1,301 Aix-Marseille University students.

benchmarks.label: Overall mean in a prior broad typing sample
benchmarks.note: The 2022 study reports that Dhakal et al. (2018) found an overall mean of 52 WPM in its sample; use as a cited benchmark, not as a universal adult average.

unavailable.reason: The attempted public URL https://www.nitrotype.com/leaderboards displayed a 404 Error page, so no leaderboard scores were included.

notes: Updated from pages read on 2026-08-04 UTC. The 15 highest current live entries are Monkeytype's readable all-time English 15-second table; they are short-test, site-reported results and are not comparable with the Guinness one-minute typewriter record. The specified TypeRacer text-details page was readable and supplied a per-text Top 10, not a current all-time or rolling global high-score board, so its entries were not mixed into the capped live list. 10FastFingers exposed a current English Normal one-minute WPM ranking without accuracy values, but its scores did not enter the overall top 15. The benchmarks are research-sample results, not global population percentiles; no defensible published percentile cutoffs were found, so percentiles is intentionally empty. The 317.443 WPM record is a TypeRacer adjusted-speed maintrack score documented by TypeRacer, not a Guinness world record.
